definition: Hypnotherapy is a form of psychotherapy carried out in trance or hypnosis by a trained therapist. In the supplied source, it is described as something that can be tailored to a person’s symptoms and combined with other psychotherapy to address related emotional or trauma-related problems.

reasons: The packet supports psychotherapy in trance and the involvement of a trained therapist, but it does not clearly define hypnotherapy as being carried out in hypnosis as well as trance.

The second sentence adds a general description of tailoring to symptoms and addressing emotional or trauma-related problems; the source only gives this as an example in severe IBS cases and clinical experience, not as a general definition of the term.

The packet discusses hypnotherapy specifically in the context of irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) and gut-directed hypnosis, but the definition presents hypnotherapy as a general form of psychotherapy without any IBS limitation.

The definition’s claim that it can be “tailored to a person’s symptoms and combined with other psychotherapy to address related emotional or trauma-related problems” is only supported by the packet in “severe cases”/“in these cases” for IBS (e.g., targeting mental comorbidities, unresolved emotional conflicts, traumatic events), not as a general feature of hypnotherapy across settings.
